opening_rules: establish material debt/home insecurity before or alongside the creature miracle
make first creature contact a life-saving care decision before economic value is used
give magical value a consent/suffering cost
keep food/work/customer proof visible as protagonist capability
risk_patterns: magic becomes free money without ethical cost
creature is adopted/possessed instead of returned to its own home or personhood
legal documents appear without being seeded in the economic world
villain only steals money rather than denying creature/child personhood
ending solves creature plot but leaves the opening housing/debt wound unpaid
thumbnail_rules: combine impossible environment contrast with intimate protector-child contact
keep faces/blanket/care readable before fantasy spectacle
use the economic world as contextual detail rather than clutter

input/reference video billing can increase cost on some providers
voice, music, edit, QA, and labor are excluded
recheck exact provider pricing/terms before any spend

validate character consistency with a cheap fixed smoke pack first
use expensive models only for hero/motion-critical shots
track actual generated seconds vs final seconds as a KPI

meaning_carrier_intelligence.opening_meaning: the vial is the last measured gift of clean rainwater left by Nura's mother
meaning_carrier_intelligence.closing_reversal: the same vial proves the land trust has been secretly diverting the town aquifer
meaning_carrier_intelligence.final_sequence_use: the object is used openly in the proof/restoration ritual before the final communal meal or work ritual in the dry pump yard transformed into a shared garden where water and food are shared by choice
meaning_carrier_intelligence.craft_rule: A physical object, space, sound-object, or ritual should carry the wound in the opening and return with changed meaning in the payoff.

fields.power_asymmetry: private resource/legal ownership versus debt-bound worker and a nonhuman child treated as property
fields.safety_or_kindness_before_power: her grandmother offers food, shelter, and patient labor before anyone powerful believes her before knowing the creature's value or any powerful ally's status
fields.costly_protagonist_action: Nura protects a child-sized moonfin creature with silver fins and a frightened singing voice at cost to her home, business, safety, and the chance to solve debt quickly
fields.consent_or_personhood_repair: the creature is never owned as a reward; authority must admit the fraud, the creature chooses home/contact, and the protagonist accepts partnership without possession
fields.payoff_image: the dry pump yard transformed into a shared garden where water and food are shared by choice; the moonfin returns to the underground spring family rather than becoming Nura's property

relational_contract_intelligence.craft_rule: Power-asymmetric relationships are strongest when safety or costly kindness precedes power, and the ending repairs consent/personhood rather than rewarding coercion.

spatial_status_intelligence.doctrine: Define who is physically forced below/outside/inside power, then make the ending transform that space into chosen access, sanctuary, or belonging. Inspired by floor/table and cage/sanctuary evidence.

closure_integrity.craft_rule: A plot sequel hook may remain, but only after the promised recognition, home, belonging, and community consequence have landed.

visual_causality.doctrine: Every scene should remain broadly intelligible when muted: visible protector/protected relation, physical action, object/space consequence, and a final image changed by the turn.
